newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Opposition say 40 killed in Taleban air raid.
newsitem.headline: Opposition say 40 killed in Taleban air raid.

text.p: An opposition commander said on Friday that a Taleban air raid on a northern town had hit a prison, killing 40 Taleban captives and wounding 30, including two Taleban ministers, a Pakistan-based Afghan news service reported.

The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) quoted General Fauzi as saying that Taleban Foreign Minister Mullah Mohammad Ghous and Civil Aviation Minister Maulvi Akhter Mohammad Mansoor were among those wounded in the raid on the town of Maimana.

AIP quoted Fauzi as saying that a total of 90 people had been killed by Taleban bombing raids on Maimana, capital of Faryab province, over the past two days, with one bomb landing near a mosque and another hitting a clinic.
A senior Taleban official, Wakil Ahmad, told AIP that the Taleban had bombed Maimana, but said the purist Islamic militia's planes had hit only military targets.
He said Taleban prisoners captured in the northern capital of Mazar-i-Sharif in late May had been moved to Maimana at one point but had later been shifted to another town, Shibergan.
There was no independent confirmation of the reported bombing raids and casualties.
